issue_context.title: todo.remove_item throws an error when item doesn't exist, cannot continue on error, cannot "upsert"
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I recently attempted to update my Shopping List based automation scripts to use the new To-do services but they behave differently.  Specifically, `todo.remove_item` throws an error when the item doesn't exist whereas `shopping_list.remove_item` does not.

This difference in behavior breaks my automation because I have been relying on the pattern of calling `shopping_list.remove_item` followed by `shopping_list.add_item` to add / update items to an incomplete state without creating duplicates.

As a work-around, I tried creating a script that attempts to remove the item with `continue_on_error: true` and then add the item back but the script still terminates on an error at the first step if the item doesn't already exist.  Perhaps the integration is throwing an error type that `continue_on_error` cannot handle.  Regardless, I'm unsure how to proceed short of continuing to use the Shopping List entity for now.

I think there should be an easier way to "upsert" (update or insert) an item to the desired state.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.12.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

todo

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/todo/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
The script I created in an attempt to use `continue_on_error` to add an item only if it doesn't exist:


alias: Add to-do item uniquely
sequence:
  - service: todo.remove_item
    target:
      entity_id: '{{ todo }}'
    data:
      item: '{{ item }}'
    continue_on_error: true
  - service: todo.add_item
    target:
      entity_id: '{{ todo }}'
    data:
      item: '{{ item }}'
mode: queued
icon: mdi:clipboard-list
fields:
  todo:
    selector:
      entity: {}
    name: To-do entity
    required: true
  item:
    selector:
      text: null
    name: Item
    required: true
```

The automation that invokes the script:

```
id: '1694329946883'
alias: 'Chore due: Feed the fish'
description: ''
trigger:
  - platform: time
    at: '06:00:00'
condition: []
action:
  - service: script.add_to_do_item_uniquely
    data:
      todo: todo.chores
      item: Feed the fish
mode: single
```
```

@j9brown using `continue_on_error` is the right way to handle this if you want it to proceed on an error even if the item does not exist. Another option is to use `get_items` and use templates to determine if the item exists and only create if it does not already. Your suggestion to allow upsert makes sense and that would be considered a feature request that can happen through the community forums. (github is used to track new issues and not really feature requests)

@omakoti can you please file a new issue and full out the full issue template? That needs to be routed to a different integration, not shopping list.
Please note that continue_on_error does not work.  The todo service is currently throwing an error that continue_on_error does not catch.
@j9brown Thanks, I missed that. I agree that is indeed a bug and I'll work on a fix for that.

There is some subtlety here, so i'll confirm that continue on error is appropriate here. There are some standards around what can be considered a "continue on error" case vs not. 

```
Please note that continue_on_error will not suppress/ignore misconfiguration or errors that Home Assistant does not handle.
```
So for example, specifying an invalid entity id is a misconfiguration, but here this needs to be treated like a possibly expected error, which is a different kind of input validation error.
